motion: Does consciousness fundamentally pervade reality and point toward God?

moves.currentDescription: Matter has no epistemic priority over directly experienced consciousness, so research cannot assume nonconscious matter as the starting point.
moves.lockedProposition: Matter has no epistemic priority over directly experienced consciousness, so research cannot assume nonconscious matter as the starting point.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Yes. I don't First of all, I would say there is no reason to privilege matter over consciousness. Um we as I say, we have direct experience of consciousness. We have indirect experience of matter because we encounter it in consciousness. Um secondly, I I understand Anil to be saying really, if I carry on researching, I will show how consciousness can emerge from matter that has no consciousness in it. I think that's what you're saying.

moves.currentDescription: Declaring the explanatory gap permanently unbridgeable projects present ignorance into a future state of much greater understanding.
moves.lockedProposition: Declaring the explanatory gap permanently unbridgeable projects present ignorance into a future state of much greater understanding.

But we don't know whether we'd be mystified in the same way by Y from the point of view where we are now of not yet understanding X.
